# Signed click token with 30-minute expiry

> A base64url JSON payload plus a truncated HMAC-SHA256 signature, verified in constant time and rejected once expired.

_Part of [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md)_

When an ad is served, a click token is generated that signs a payload containing the impression id, campaign id, shop id, price, and a 30-minute expiry. The token is a compact string: `payload.mac` where the payload is the base64url-encoded claims and the mac is a truncated HMAC-SHA256 signature. When a user clicks and sends the token to the backend in [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md), the server calls [`verifyClick`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) to recompute the signature in constant time, decode the claims, and reject the token if it's expired. This stateless check proves the impression was real and hasn't been forged.

**Look at:** [click-token.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/domain/click-token.ts)

## Pieces

- Click token payload (ClickClaims): The fields signed into every token: impression id (`i`), campaign id (`c`), shop id (`s`), price (`p`), and expiry timestamp (`e`).
- [Creating a signed token (signClick)](sign-click.md): Encodes the claims as base64url JSON and appends a truncated HMAC-SHA256 signature in the format `payload.mac`.
- [Validating a signed token (verifyClick)](verify-click.md): Recomputes the signature in constant time, decodes the claims, and rejects the token if expired.

## Watch out

- The expiry time `e` is a millisecond timestamp set when signing; [`verifyClick`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) rejects tokens where e <= now.
- The signature is truncated to 32 base64url characters (~24 bytes of decoded data) to keep tokens short; the full HMAC-SHA256 is 256 bits, so 192 bits remains strong.
- There is no server-side state: tokens are verified using only the signing secret, so no database or cache lookup is needed—fast and stateless.
- `timingSafeEqual` prevents timing attacks that could leak information about the signature through response latency differences.
